name: Oyster Catsup
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Procure the oysters very fresh and open sufficient to fill a pint measure; save the liquor and scald the oysters in it with the sherry.
Strain the oysters and chop them fine with the salt, cayenne and mace, until reduced to a pulp; then add it to the liquor in which they were scalded.
Boil it again five minutes and skim well; rub the whole through a sieve, and, when cold, bottle and cork closely.

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Procure the oysters very fresh and open sufficient to fill a pint measure; save the liquor and scald the oysters in it with the sherry.
2. Strain the oysters and chop them fine with the salt, cayenne and mace, until reduced to a pulp; then add it to the liquor in which they were scalded.
3. Boil it again five minutes and skim well; rub the whole through a sieve, and, when cold, bottle and cork closely.
4. The corks should be sealed.
